input_signals.name: Profitable Intangible Intensity Product
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible intensity is rewarded only when the firm is already profitable; the joint condition (high operating profitability AND high R&D+advertising intensity) identifies firms whose expensed investment is productive but whose book assets understate capital.
input_signals.reasoning: The multiplicative form is a true conditional interaction: it is large only where both industry-relative ranks are high and collapses when either leg fails, unlike an additive composite that can be carried by one theme alone. Industry ranking neutralizes the mechanical clustering of R&D and advertising intensity in a few sectors.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), sale ) ) )

input_signals.name: Persistently Profitable Innovator
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ib, at), 0), 5), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible intensity is rewarded only when profitability has been repeatedly demonstrated; the count of profitable years over five years is the cleanest validation that the expensed investment base is productive, so persistent profitability times intangible intensity identifies the underpriced group.
input_signals.reasoning: The profitability leg is a 0-to-5 persistence count rather than a contemporaneous level, which distinguishes durably productive intangible capital from one-year earnings noise and avoids simply re-summing two published effects. The multiplicative form means chronic loss-makers score zero regardless of how much they spend, so the long-short spread is driven by the interaction rather than by either theme in isolation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ts_sum( indicator( ratio( ib, at ), 0 ), 5 ), ind_rank( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), sale ) ) )

input_signals.name: Brand Capital Pricing Power
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, sale)), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(xad, 3), sale)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Advertising builds brand capital that is fully expensed; when accumulated brand investment coexists with high operating margins, the pricing power is proof that the expensed brand asset is real and productive, yet book assets record none of it.
input_signals.reasoning: Every prior evaluated signal ran the intangible leg through R&D, so this tests whether the mechanism generalizes to the brand channel, where validation should show up in margin (pricing power) rather than in return on assets. Advertising is only reported by a subset of firms, so raw `xad` is used deliberately to define the signal on the population where brand capital is economically meaningful rather than diluting it with zeros.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, sale ) ), ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( xad, 3 ), sale ) ) )

input_signals.name: Stable Earnings Intangible Capital
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Investors apply a uniform uncertainty discount to intangible-intensive firms; those whose realized operating profitability has been stable for five years have demonstrably low-risk intangible capital, so the discount is unwarranted and their returns are too high.
input_signals.reasoning: This changes the validation variable from the *level* of profitability (used by every gen-0 survivor) to its *second moment*, testing a risk-misperception channel rather than a level-mispricing channel — an informative discrimination between mechanisms. Both legs are non-negative industry ranks, so the product is high only for the stable-and-intangible-heavy quadrant the hypothesis names.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( oiadp, at ), 5 ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( add( coalesce( intan, 0 ), ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Payback Among Intangible Heavy Firms
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Validated intangible productivity requires two things simultaneously: a materially large intangible capital base and a high operating profit earned per dollar of that base; firms satisfying both have proven their off-balance-sheet capital works, while the market prices them off reported assets.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the degenerate composition share with a payback rate supplies the magnitude anchor the critic wanted, and the MIN operator (a strict AND rather than a product) forces both legs to be high, which neutralizes the mechanical tilt of any payback ratio toward firms with negligible intangible capital. The intensity leg also acts as the economic screen the earlier version lacked, so the signal is defined on firms with a genuine intangible base rather than on 0/0 cases.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( oiadp, add( coalesce( intan, 0 ), ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( add( coalesce( intan, 0 ), ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Organization Capital Efficiency Of Intangible Firms
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: SG&A is the expensed outlay that builds organization, distribution and human capital; gross profit earned per dollar of SG&A measures how productive that organizational capital is, and this productivity should be most mispriced at firms whose overall asset base is already intangible-heavy.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the capitalized-R&D replacement-capital ratio the critic identified as a rediscovery and switches the profitability channel to SG&A efficiency, a distinct productivity construct not represented anywhere in the archive. The interaction is real: SG&A efficiency alone is an operating-leverage measure, but conditioned on a large intangible base it becomes evidence that the firm's expensed investments are generating profit that never appears on the balance sheet.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), xsga ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( add( coalesce( intan, 0 ), ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Amortization Drag On Intangible Earnings
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(dp, at), RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with large booked intangibles and a heavy depreciation-and-amortization charge report GAAP earnings that are depressed by non-cash write-offs of assets that are still productive; investors anchoring on bottom-line earnings undervalue those firms whose pre-amortization operating profitability is strong.
input_signals.reasoning: The conditioning variable is now the product of D&A intensity and booked-intangible intensity, which localizes the measure to firms where amortization of intangibles is plausibly the dominant non-cash charge, instead of the total-accrual wedge that reduced the prior version to a Sloan variant. Pairing it with pre-amortization operating profitability (oibdp) makes the mechanism explicit: high cash-level earning power that GAAP earnings understate.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ind_rank( winsor( mul( ratio( dp, at ), ratio( coalesce( intan, 0 ), at ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Profitable Goodwill Impairer
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), 1), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A goodwill write-down is a backward-looking non-cash charge that removes an already-paid-for intangible from the books; when the firm continues to generate strong operating cash flow, the impairment has cleaned the balance sheet without impairing the business, yet earnings-anchored investors mark the stock down.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the organic-minus-acquired composition family entirely and tests the *event* through which capitalized intangibles are removed, using the direction of goodwill change rather than its level, so it does not re-tread the archived contrast. The interaction is essential: an impairment with collapsing cash flow is genuine bad news, while an impairment with intact cash generation is an accounting correction, and only their combination identifies the mispriced group.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oancf, at ) ), ind_rank( neg( winsor( ratio( delta( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), 1 ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accounting Conservatism Intensity
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), dp), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The ratio of expensed intangible outlays to recorded depreciation and amortization measures how much of a firm's total investment bypasses the asset base entirely; profitable firms with the most conservative accounting have the largest gap between their economic and reported capital and are therefore the most undervalued.
input_signals.reasoning: The conditioning variable is a within-firm comparison of capitalized versus expensed investment flows rather than an intangible-intensity level, so it directly quantifies the accounting distortion the theme's story rests on instead of proxying it with R&D scaled by sales. It replaces the artifact-prone 0/1 profitability gate with a continuous, fully covered rank and, unlike the flagged version, its cross-sectional variation comes from a measure with no published anomaly counterpart.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), dp ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Invention Commercialization Complementarity
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ib, at)), MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xad, 0), sale))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Knowledge capital only earns rents when it is commercialized, so R&D and advertising are economic complements; firms that invest meaningfully in both and are already profitable have a complete, proven intangible production chain that the accounts record nowhere.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archived intangible leg added R&D and advertising together, which lets a pure R&D spender or a pure advertiser reach the top decile; the MIN operator instead requires both channels simultaneously, testing complementarity across intangible types rather than substituting one profitability measure for another. This is a different economic claim from the gen-0 winner, and comparing the two also isolates whether SUM or AND is the right aggregation of intangible inputs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ib, at ) ), min( ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ) ), ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( xad, 0 ), sale ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Hidden Equity Relative To Book Net Worth
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ib, ceq)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(ceq, COALESCE(intan, 0))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Book equity, not total assets, is the anchor investors use for valuation; firms whose unrecorded knowledge capital is large relative to their recorded net worth have the most understated book value, and when they simultaneously earn a high return on that understated equity the mispricing is largest.
input_signals.reasoning: Rescaling both legs from assets to book equity changes the economic claim from "the asset base is understated" to "the valuation anchor is understated," and the return-on-equity leg is mechanically inflated by the same accounting conservatism, which is precisely why the interaction rather than either leg alone identifies mispricing. It is not a screened restatement of the gen-0 winner: no hard gate creates a zero mass, and the intangible leg is a hidden-capital-to-net-worth ratio rather than a spending intensity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ib, ceq ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), add( ceq, coalesce( intan, 0 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Validated Intangible Write Down
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(intan, 0), 1), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Shrinking the booked intangible balance — through impairment or amortization run-off — removes overstated purchased capital from the accounts; when operating cash flow is simultaneously strong, the write-down is an accounting correction rather than economic deterioration, and earnings-anchored investors overreact to it.
input_signals.reasoning: The goodwill version of this mechanism produced the archive's strongest Fama-MacBeth slope (4.13) and best Sharpe (0.29) but its alpha t-stat was held back by 0.084 coverage; broadening the write-down measure from goodwill to all booked intangibles roughly doubles the eligible sample while preserving the identical economic event. If the alpha t-stat rises with coverage, the earlier weakness was statistical rather than economic, which is a decisive piece of information for the remaining generations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oancf, at ) ), ind_rank( neg( winsor( ratio( delta( coalesce( intan, 0 ), 1 ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accumulated Expensing Distortion
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), TS_SUM(dp, 5)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The gap between economic and book capital is a stock that builds up over years of expensing, so the five-year cumulative ratio of expensed intangible outlays to cumulative depreciation measures how far the balance sheet has actually drifted from economic capital, and profitable firms with the largest accumulated drift are the most underpriced.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike the bounded-share version, a five-year cumulative ratio is not a monotone transform of the one-year ratio: it reorders firms whose current-year investment mix is unrepresentative of their sustained policy and it isolates the accumulated distortion the hypothesis is actually about. Multi-year sums also damp the small-denominator instability and annual turnover of the archived one-year conservatism measure, which should show up as a higher alpha t-stat and Sharpe rather than a higher raw alpha alone.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 5 ), ts_sum( dp, 5 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Balance Sheet Light Intangible Shift
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(GROWTH(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 1), GROWTH(at, 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitable firms that are expanding expensed intangible investment faster than their recorded asset base are actively reallocating capital from assets investors can see to assets they cannot, so the measurement gap widens exactly when the firm's growth is real but invisible.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the ensembling of two archive winners with a single new quantity — the divergence between intangible-investment growth and balance-sheet growth — which no prior signal measures and which cannot be produced by averaging existing ranks. It also distinguishes the theme's mechanism from the asset-growth anomaly: the long leg is firms with *low* asset growth and *high* intangible growth, so a positive result attributes the alpha to the accounting gap rather than to shrinking investment alone.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ind_rank( winsor( sub( growth( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 1 ), growth( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Downside Earning Power Of Distorted Firms
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), dp), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible capital earns durable rents only if it protects profits in bad years; a firm whose *worst* profitability over five years is still high has a moat, and combining that proof of durability with a large accounting distortion identifies the most reliably underpriced innovators.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive has tested the level, trend, persistence-count and volatility of profitability as validation legs, but never the worst-case level, which is the measure a rational investor would use to judge whether hidden capital is genuinely productive rather than cyclically lucky. Because TS_MIN is a downside statistic it should also concentrate the long leg in firms whose FF5 profitability loading is stable, addressing the RMW-absorption problem that flattened several earlier slopes.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( oiadp, at ), 5 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), dp ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Off Books Capital Formation
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), DELTA(COALESCE(intan, 0), 1)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The net rate at which a firm adds capital that the balance sheet will never record equals its expensed intangible outlays minus the increase in booked intangibles; cash-profitable firms with the highest net off-books capital formation are compounding invisible assets fastest.
input_signals.reasoning: This fuses the two winning ideas into one economic quantity rather than averaging two correlated ranks: a firm that spends heavily on R&D and advertising while its booked intangible balance shrinks is unambiguously moving capital off the balance sheet, whereas a firm capitalizing acquisitions is doing the opposite. Cash flow rather than accrual profit is the validation leg because the same accounting that hides the asset also distorts the earnings line.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oancf, at ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), delta( coalesce( intan, 0 ), 1 ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Conversion Of Innovator Profits
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, MAX(oibdp, dp)), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible-intensive firms report earnings that are heavily distorted by expensing and accrual timing, so the trustworthy validation of hidden-asset productivity is the fraction of operating profit that arrives as cash; innovators with high cash conversion have real, not accounting, profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests earnings *quality* rather than earnings level as the validating condition, a channel absent from the archive and economically distinct from cash-based profitability because it is a ratio of cash to accrual profit rather than a scaled profit level. Flooring the denominator at depreciation keeps the conversion ratio well behaved for loss-making firms, avoiding the sign-flip defect that undermined the earlier interest-coverage construction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( oancf, max( oibdp, dp ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), sale ) ) )

input_signals.name: Distortion Large In Both Dimensions
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), dp), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm's book capital is materially understated only when its expensed intangible outlay is large both relative to the investment it does capitalize and relative to its overall asset base; profitable firms meeting both conditions have genuinely, not mechanically, distorted accounts.
input_signals.reasoning: The archived conservatism winner can be topped out by asset-light firms with negligible depreciation and only trivial R&D, a small-denominator route into the long leg that has nothing to do with hidden capital; the MIN requires an economically large absolute intangible outlay before the ratio counts. This is a construction repair of the best signal in the archive rather than a numerator swap, and it should raise ls_talpha and Sharpe by removing an unstable subset of long-leg names.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), min( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), dp ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Marginal Return On Matured Intangible Spending
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, LAG(oiadp, 3)), LAG(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), 1)), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Validated intangible productivity is a marginal return: the dollars of extra operating profit earned over three years per dollar of intangible investment made in the preceding three years, realized by firms that are genuinely intangible-intensive.
input_signals.reasoning: Both numerator and denominator are dollar flows over matched, non-overlapping windows, so no current-sales scaler sneaks a growth term in, and the quantity is a payback rate rather than a persistent intensity level that would be collinear with the gen-0 winner's contemporaneous leg. The MIN with intensity blocks the mechanical tilt toward low-spending firms that a payback ratio would otherwise produce, which was the flaw in the gen-0 version of this idea.

input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( oiadp, lag( oiadp, 3 ) ), lag( ts_sum( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 3 ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), sale ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Spending At Its Own Peak
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), TS_MAX(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A profitable firm still spending at its five-year peak on R&D and advertising is building hidden capital, whereas one that has retreated from its own peak is harvesting an ageing intangible base; the market reads current earnings identically in both cases.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the mirror-image acquirer test with a self-normalized commitment state that is bounded in [0,1], which is exactly the fix suggested by the archive's pattern that growth-rate intangible legs generate slopes but no FF5 alpha because they load on the investment factor. Because the ratio is measured against the firm's own history rather than the cross-section, it is orthogonal to industry intangible intensity and tests pipeline continuation rather than spending level.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), ts_max( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 5 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Off Books Share Of Capital Formation
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), DELTA(COALESCE(intan, 0), 1)), ADD(dp, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: What matters is not the dollar amount of off-books capital formation but the fraction of the firm's total capital formation that never reaches the balance sheet, net of anything it capitalizes; cash-profitable firms with the highest such fraction have the fastest-growing invisible asset base.
input_signals.reasoning: The critic's concern about the gen-4 leader was that scaling by assets lets the persistent R&D/at component dominate; rescaling by the firm's own total investment (depreciation plus expensed intangible outlay) removes the size-intensity component and leaves a pure composition-of-investment measure. The denominator is strictly positive by construction, so the ratio is well behaved, and if alpha survives this rescaling the mechanism is the accounting composition rather than R&D intensity in disguise.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oancf, at ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), delta( coalesce( intan, 0 ), 1 ) ), add( dp, add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Pre Investment Cash Earning Power
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), dp), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Because intangible outlays are expensed, they depress operating cash flow exactly as they depress earnings; adding them back reveals the firm's true cash earning power before discretionary investment, and firms with high pre-investment cash power that also run the largest expensing distortion are the most severely mismeasured.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archived validation leg measures profitability *after* the intangible spending that the theme argues is really investment, which systematically penalizes the very firms the hypothesis targets; restoring the outlay makes the profitability and distortion legs economically consistent for the first time. This is a different quantity from cash-based profitability — it is capacity to fund hidden investment rather than residual cash — and it cannot be produced by rescaling any existing signal.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( add( oancf, add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ), at ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), dp ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual Validated Off Books Formation
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), DELTA(COALESCE(intan, 0), 1)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: If off-books capital formation is what carries the alpha, it should predict returns when validated by accrual operating profitability as well; if instead the effect requires cash-flow validation, the cash leg is doing the economic work rather than the intangible composition.

Holding the intangible leg exactly fixed and swapping only the validator answers that question directly, and the answer dictates whether the final consolidated signal should accept the coverage cost of `oancf`.
